clue.text: Ring everyone in competition

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, as in the FA Cup
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A tournament organiser telephoning every entrant in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like part of the wordplay, but it is the definition, in its telephone sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up someone is to telephone them, the same as giving them a ring.

clue.text: Crew's leader is indebted to yachting centre

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of crew
someone indebted owes

explanation.surface: A boat's crew-leader runs up debts at a sailing resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes, on the Isle of Wight off England's south coast, is home to the famous Cowes Week regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is world-renowned as a hub of sailing and yacht racing, hence a centre for the sport.

clue.text: Fib about information that's turned up involving a pedigree

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a fib is a lie

indicators.note: in a down entry, something turned up reads from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
one thing placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lie told about some reversed facts concerning a pedigree animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; 'pedigree' at the end is the definition, not part of the fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineage is a line of descent from ancestors, which is what a pedigree records.

clue.text: Riding team losing in a chaotic manner

parts.note: a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up
a side is a team
a team that is losing is down, as in two goals down

explanation.surface: An equestrian team falling behind and riding in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding team' reads as one unit, but it splits: a jockey 'up' is riding, and a side is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned upside down is in total disorder, the idiom for a chaotic mess.

clue.text: Quarrel pettily about temperature, and refuse to change one's opinion

indicators.note: something put about other letters goes round them, enclosing them

parts.note: to spat is to have a petty quarrel
T is the abbreviation for temperature
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bickering over the thermostat setting and refusing to back down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' that seems to join two halves of the sentence is itself part of what goes inside SPAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pat is an idiom from poker for keeping one's hand, hence sticking firmly to a position.

clue.text: Film mislaid during Saturday and Sunday?

definitions.text: Film mislaid during Saturday and Sunday?

parts.words: Film mislaid during Saturday and Sunday?
parts.note: surface reading: a reel of film gets lost somewhere over the weekend
setter's reading: a weekend that has gone missing gives the title of a 1945 film

explanation.surface: Someone misplaced a roll of film over the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1945 Billy Wilder film, about an alcoholic's lost days of drinking, is described literally as a weekend that went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of an Oscar-winning movie, read here as a description of time that disappeared.

clue.text: Pond creature recently discovered on top of tank

parts.note: something recently discovered is new

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of tank

explanation.surface: A newly found creature sitting on top of a fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The newt is a small amphibian that breeds in ponds, so it is a typical pond animal.

clue.text: A spice in mash served with raki abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food
raki is an aniseed spirit from Turkey; its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seasoning a mash eaten with a glass of raki on holiday overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' fits the travel scene of drinking raki, but it signals rearranging those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a red powdered seasoning made from dried peppers, a common spice.

clue.text: Take turns flying in part of Asia

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pilots alternating at the controls on a flight over Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkestan is a historical region of Central Asia, so it is a portion of the continent.

clue.text: Register in seaside accommodation, say, that's basic

indicators.note: words placed in a phrase go inside it, splitting it open

parts.note: a B and B is a bed and breakfast, typical seaside lodging
a meter registers or reads a value
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Signing the register at a seaside guest house, the most basic kind of stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A B and B is a bed and breakfast; each B is opened, the register reading going after the first and the saying after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter is an idiom for the everyday, fundamental part of something, hence basic.

clue.text: Motorised device inspired new crew at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A motor-powered gadget that motivated a fresh team of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' looks like a verb with the device as its subject, but it is just letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A windscreen wiper is driven by a small electric motor, so it is a motor-powered device on a car.

clue.text: Photograph monster flower

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a monstrous bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden plant whose blossoms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Fish pie containing last of haddock

indicators.note: one word containing another holds it within its letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter alone

parts.note: final letter of haddock

explanation.surface: A fish pie with a bit of haddock in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish pie' reads as one dish, but 'Fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a predatory freshwater fish with a long snout.

clue.text: Such a lie is much worse than a bad one, of course

definitions.text: Such a lie is much worse than a bad one, of course

parts.words: Such a lie is much worse than a bad one
parts.note: surface reading: some untruths are far more damaging than others
setter's reading: on a golf course, the lie is where the ball comes to rest, and the worst lie cannot be hit at all

explanation.surface: A moral remark that some falsehoods are worse than others, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' means a falsehood in the surface but a ball's resting position in golf; 'of course' signals the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer can declare a ball unplayable when it lies where no stroke is possible, taking a penalty drop.

clue.text: Head of depot to study alarm

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of depot
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A depot manager about to examine an alarm system.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread and alarm are both nouns for a state of fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Supplanted theologian catching special broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered into a new order
catching something means holding it inside

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, the theologian's degree
the letters of special, rearranged

explanation.surface: A theologian ousted after being caught out by a special programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special broadcast' reads as a TV special, but broadcast tells you to rearrange the letters of special.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone supplanted has been displaced, pushed out of their position by another.

clue.text: Helper to accompany worker

parts.note: to attend someone is to accompany them
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An assistant going along with a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is an assistant or servant who waits on others.

clue.text: One may help one to escape from a trap

definitions.text: One may help one to escape from a trap

parts.words: One may help one to escape from a trap
parts.note: surface reading: someone or something that frees a person who is caught or ensnared
setter's reading: a sand trap is a golf bunker, and a particular club is designed for hitting out of it

explanation.surface: Someone who aids a person in getting free of a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap here is a golf bunker, the American name being sand trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand wedge is a lofted golf club built to splash the ball out of bunkers.

clue.text: Strips of pasta — last in canteen gets lots

indicators.note: the last in a word is only its final letter

parts.note: final letter of canteen
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: The final diner in the canteen gets a huge helping of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long thin ribbons of pasta or dough.

clue.text: Become aware of Liverpool's initial win

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a name

parts.note: first letter of Liverpool
to win wages is to earn them

explanation.surface: Finding out that Liverpool took the opening victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win' looks like a football result, but here it is the verb earn, as in winning one's bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to find it out, that is, to come to know of it.

clue.text: A supporter's carrying a cross that shows a word of unknown significance

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written
a bra is a supporter, plus the S of the possessive
X is a cross
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporter bearing a cross with a mysterious word on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross and the article go into BRAS as X then A, the reverse of the clue's 'a cross'. Abraxas is a Gnostic word found on amulets, of uncertain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraxas is a mystical term carved on ancient charms whose true meaning is unknown.

clue.text: Inspect king after card game

indicators.note: coming after another word means being placed behind it

parts.note: loo is an old card game
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Checking the king that turned up after a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a 17th-century trick-taking card game, not the British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to examine or inspect it.

clue.text: Red after country dance?

indicators.note: one word after another is placed behind it

parts.note: Turkey is a country
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a far-left Red

explanation.surface: A communist pursuing a nation, with a question mark hinting at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot is a ragtime ballroom dance popular in the early 20th century.

clue.text: Irritable, first in yard after exam

indicators.note: placed after means put behind the other piece

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the first in a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of yard

explanation.surface: Feeling cranky out in the yard once the exam was over.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy is a synonym for irritable, quick to lose patience.

clue.text: One was first put up in shop

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up sends it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
someone who was first led

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to be set up in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats and fine foods.

clue.text: Often filled with bread, a naturalist may use them in the field

definitions.text: Often filled with bread, a naturalist may use them in the field

parts.note: surface reading: containers for packed lunches; setter's reading: bread is slang for money, which charity tins are filled with

parts.words: a naturalist may use them in the field
parts.note: a naturalist gathering specimens outdoors keeps them in boxes

explanation.surface: Lunchboxes full of sandwiches carried by a naturalist on a field trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money: charity collectors rattle these, and the same name describes a naturalist's specimen boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both charity tins for donations and boxes used for gathering specimens.

clue.text: Files showing one occupied by vagrants? Just the opposite

indicators.note: a place occupied by people has them inside it
the opposite of being occupied is occupying, so the roles swap and the vagrants hold it

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a tramp who sleeps rough
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Folders revealing a person who is lodged among tramps, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, one would hold the vagrants; 'Just the opposite' flips it so I goes inside DOSSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dossiers are collections of documents on a subject, the same as files.

clue.text: Spirited one kept in iron pen

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, between the surrounding pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
I is the Roman numeral one
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A lively animal confined in an iron enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Feisty describes a lively, determined, combative character, full of spirit.
